text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- Creditanstalt chief Guido Schmidt-Chiari said he was confident the bidder consortium led by EA-Generali would propose an offer for the bank by Friday, the deadline set by Finance Minister Viktor Klima.
- Austria's unemployment rate remained steady in August at 4.1 percent. However the number of unemployed rose by 3,078 to 189,999 compared to the previous month.

- The top Social Democratic candidate for the European Parliamentary elections on October 13, Hannes Swoboda, has agreed with conservative Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel that all members of the European Union have to assist each other in case of a military attack.
- If Commerzbank withdraws from a consortium bidding for Creditanstalt bank, Die Erste bank might consider taking over its stake through a convertible bond, unnamed sources said.
- Austrian banks Creditanstalt, Raiffeisen and GiroCredit are setting up a holding company to fund Austrian tourism projects.
- Paper and cardboard producer Mayr-Melnhof is raising its stake in box maker Falpa to 85 percent from 50 percent.

- Cement maker Perlmooser reported operating profit was up by one million schillings to 25 million schillings in the first half of this year. Turnover dipped to 621 million schillings from 758 million. Increased sales are expected within the year.

- Austrian exports to Russia dropped by 36 percent to $343.5 million in the first half this year. Especially the campaign season for this year's Russian presidential elections caused Russian imports to fall.

- The bidder consortium interested in taking over the government's stake in Creditanstalt-Bankverein may be having troubles staying together, banking sources say. Die Erste bank's role was particularly cast into question.
